intent_en: Show that between 1990 and 2017, Sub-Saharan Africa's illiteracy rate fell more slowly, in proportional terms, than in Latin America & Caribbean, East Asia & Pacific, and the European Union.
previous_intent: To illustrate that Sub-Saharan Africa lags behind other global regions in educational progress, as evidenced by a significantly higher illiteracy rate compared to other areas.
narration_support: But especially in sub-Saharan Africa, education has improved slower than in other parts of the world.
chart_support: Bar chart displaying Illiteracy Rate 2017 for population 15 and older, showing Sub-Saharan Africa has a substantially higher rate than Latin America & Caribbean, East Asia & Pacific, and the European Union.
evidence_note: The narration provides the context of slower educational improvement, while the chart provides a snapshot of high illiteracy rates in 2017 for Sub-Saharan Africa relative to other regions, supporting the claim of lagging educational outcomes.
narrative_goal: To illustrate that Sub-Saharan Africa lags behind other global regions in educational progress, as evidenced by a significantly higher illiteracy rate compared to other areas.
